sentences.text: Fukuititan is described as a medium-sized sauropod, though some sources characterize it as a relatively small dinosaur with a total length of 10 meters.

This genus is distinguished from other titanosauriforms by stalk-like epipophyses on its cervical vertebrae, a wide humerus where the top width is 32% of its length, and metacarpals that are half the length of the radius.

The holotype includes a tooth featuring an asymmetric dental crown with an absent or weak external groove and no internal cavity, alongside a partial skeleton containing cervical vertebrae, shoulder blades, arm bones, leg bones, and three tail vertebrae.
Subsequent authors have estimated Fukuititan to be 16.1 meters long, 5.75 meters tall at the shoulder, and weigh 5.75 tons.
Fukuititan represents the first relatively complete titanosauriform skeleton found in Japan.

Fukuititan is a sauropod dinosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous found in the Kitadani Formation in modern-day Japan, where fossils were discovered in summer 2007 at the Kitadani Dinosaur Quarry near the Sugiyama River.

The only known specimen, holotype FPDM-V8468, was described in 2010 by Japanese scientists Yoichi Azuma and Masateru Shibata after being found in Kitadani in 2006 and excavated from July 2007 to summer 2008.
The unique features of the tooth suggest specific adaptations for its diet.
Features of the tail vertebrae and fused ischia support classifying Fukuititan within Titanosauriformes, primarily because its tail vertebrae resemble those of the Asian species Borealosaurus.
Fukuititan lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia, with a more precise range between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.

Gregory S. Paul suggested that the Fukuititan holotype represents an immature individual, meaning concrete adult size estimates may not be possible, and some phylogenetic analyses omit Fukuititan because its incomplete fossil record makes its classification unstable.
